clue.text: Oil worker changing oven after refurb, keeping the box

indicators.note: the rebuilt letters hold the next piece within them
a refurb is a makeover, so the letters of these two words come out rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A worker gets the kitchen oven changed after a refurbishment, holding on to the box it came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil worker' looks like someone on a rig; it means a painter in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch artist painted in oils, so he is literally a worker in oil paint.

clue.text: Unify people, target Nixon reversed to some extent

indicators.note: the hidden run is then read from right to left
only part of the run of letters across these words is used

parts.note: the letters lie across the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A call to bring people together by aiming at Nixon, reversing his policies somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into one whole, a synonym of unify.

clue.text: Sea creatures start to realise fossil fuel sucks

indicators.note: the fuel draws a letter inside itself, as if sucking it in

parts.note: coal is the classic fossil fuel

parts.note: the opening letter of this word is the one taken

explanation.surface: Marine life begins to realise that burning fossil fuel is bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucks' reads as slang for 'is terrible', which suits the eco surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral consists of colonies of tiny marine animals, polyps, so it is a mass of sea creatures.

clue.text: Sleep too long, keeping 'chronic fatigue' sign on the door

indicators.note: the short sleep holds the illness abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
ME (myalgic encephalomyelitis) is the condition also called chronic fatigue syndrome
late means after the proper time, having gone on too long

explanation.surface: Someone with chronic fatigue oversleeps and hangs a warning sign on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a small plaque on a door showing who occupies the room.

clue.text: Last bit of malt in bottle needed badly

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the small bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the closing letter of this word is the one taken

explanation.surface: A drinker urgently needs the last drop of malt whisky in the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' reads as a comment on the drinker; it is part of the definition, meaning very much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is essential, so it is needed very much indeed.

clue.text: No light in Peter's home

parts.note: 'never!' is an emphatic no
to light on something is to land or settle on it

explanation.surface: Peter's house has no light at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb, to come down and settle.
explanation.definitionFit: In J. M. Barrie's story, Peter Pan lives on the island of Neverland with the Lost Boys.

clue.text: Sons departing become tender, usually

indicators.note: the sons leave, so their letter is taken away

parts.note: to soften is to become tender

explanation.surface: When the sons leave home, a parent tends to grow soft-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and usually both describe something happening frequently, as a matter of habit; they are near-synonyms.

clue.text: Corporal punishments kept secret in Grammar School

parts.note: to hide something is to keep it secret
taken as written

explanation.surface: Canings were quietly covered up at a grammar school.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a British selective state secondary school, the old home of caning.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a thrashing, so hidings are physical beatings given as punishment.

clue.text: Creator of true likeness showed up painter

parts.note: came means arrived, turned up
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.definitionFit: A camera records exactly what is in front of it, so it produces a faithful image.

clue.text: Wally loses weight for doctor

indicators.note: the name drops the letter for weight

parts.note: Wally is a pet form of Walter

explanation.surface: Wally slims down for the sake of his doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a wally is also a fool, which makes the name look like an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with it, so it means change or modify.

clue.text: Ply date with Vimto, feeling an urge

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Vimto is a British fruit-flavoured soft drink. 'Ply' reads as offering someone drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motivated means having a drive or desire to act.

clue.text: Drink that's mixed for one girlfriend with sauce

clue.text: Possibly reading in diary, Pierre's no spectacles

non is French for no, and Pierre is a typical Frenchman

explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnon is a pair of eyeglasses, such as a lorgnette or pince-nez, held up to the eyes.

clue.text: Third term president America prevents from running

parts.note: a dam stops water flowing, so dams means stops something running

explanation.surface: America stops a president from standing for a third term.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington served two terms, so John Adams, his successor, held the third presidential term.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams was the second US president, holding office in the nation's third presidential term after Washington's two.

clue.text: Post from China's not interfered with

explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright bar or support, a kind of post.

clue.text: Risk judges covering court with gold stars?

indicators.note: the gold goes around the court abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

clue.text: Silly chicken guards local grain store

clue.text: Guy's drug gets rid of cold without delay

parts.note: to medicate is to drug someone

clue.text: Before Dell, books commonly used

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

clue.text: A little shellfish Spanish footballers brought up after training

clue.text: The people protest, with NHS scrapping new hospital

clue.text: Dismayed finding tin full of fish

clue.text: Full marks on Strictly, couple finally perfect?
